cast.name: The Listener
cast.role: the contemporary listener facing a big choice: a job offer, a house, a hire, a launch, a partnership
cast.look: A 34-year-old American professional with short dark brown hair, wearing a teal casual button-up shirt and grey chinos.

cast.name: Charles Darwin
cast.role: naturalist who weighs marriage on a two-column list in 1838, and later weighs publishing his theory against his wife's faith
cast.look: A Victorian English gentleman of about 30 with a receding hairline, brown muttonchop sideburns, a black frock coat and white high collar.

cast.name: Emma Darwin
cast.role: Darwin's wife, whose faith after their daughter's death his theory would wound
cast.look: A Victorian Englishwoman in her thirties with dark hair parted in the middle in a low bun, wearing a deep plum high-necked dress.

cast.name: Benjamin Franklin
cast.role: invents 'moral algebra' in a 1772 letter to Priestley
cast.look: An elderly 18th-century American statesman, balding with long grey hair at the sides, small round spectacles, brown wool coat.

cast.name: Joseph Priestley
cast.role: scientist agonizing over a job offer from the Earl of Shelburne; Franklin's friend
cast.look: An 18th-century English clergyman-scientist of about 40 with short brown hair, a plain black coat and a white clerical neckband.

cast.name: Pierre L'Enfant
cast.role: French architect who proposes cleaning Collect Pond and making it a public park
cast.look: A French architect of about 50 in 1802, dark hair tied back, navy blue tailcoat with a rolled plan under his arm.

cast.name: The City Council
cast.role: the 1802 New York council and developers who reduce Collect Pond to a binary and fill it in
cast.look: A stout New York merchant-alderman of 1802 with grey sideburns, black top hat and a mustard waistcoat under a dark coat.

cast.name: John Brennan
cast.role: counterterrorism adviser who demands the analysts disprove their own theory
cast.look: A balding American official in his fifties with short grey hair at the sides, a charcoal suit, white shirt and dark red tie.

cast.name: The CIA Analyst
cast.role: intelligence analyst mapping the Abbottabad compound and building the case
cast.look: A 38-year-old woman analyst with a dark brown ponytail, glasses, a light blue blouse under a navy cardigan and an ID badge.

cast.name: The CEO
cast.role: the boss at the head of the table whom everyone agrees with too quickly
cast.look: A confident man of 55 with slicked silver hair in a navy three-piece suit and light blue tie.

cast.name: The Dissenting Colleague
cast.role: the cognitively peripheral voice in the room: holds the unshared fact, a juror from a different background
cast.look: A 30-year-old Black woman with natural curly hair, wearing a mustard yellow blazer over a black top.

cast.name: Steven Johnson
cast.role: the author, weighing a move from Brooklyn to Marin County with his wife
cast.look: An American writer around 45 with short sandy-brown hair, light stubble and glasses, wearing a green flannel shirt.

cast.name: Johnson's Wife
cast.role: weighs her Brooklyn friendships against California
cast.look: A woman around 45 with shoulder-length auburn hair, wearing a burgundy sweater and dark jeans.

cast.name: George Eliot
cast.role: Victorian novelist writing Middlemarch at her desk
cast.look: A Victorian Englishwoman of about 50 with brown hair parted in the centre over the ears, wearing a dark grey dress with a white lace collar.

cast.name: Dorothea Brooke
cast.role: Middlemarch's idealistic heroine choosing whether to marry Casaubon
cast.look: A young Victorian woman of 19 with dark chestnut hair in braids, wearing a plain pale lavender dress.

cast.name: Mr. Casaubon
cast.role: the dry, pedantic old scholar Dorothea is drawn to marry
cast.look: A gaunt Victorian scholar of about 50 with thin white hair, a black scholar's coat and a book always in hand.
